purpose: Butoconazole nitrate is used to treat vaginal yeast infections caused by a fungus called Candida. It helps relieve uncomfortable symptoms like itching, burning, and discharge. It is available as a vaginal cream that you apply inside the vagina.
how_it_works: This medication works by attacking the outer protective layer of the yeast fungus, essentially poking holes in it. Without that protective layer, the fungus cannot survive and dies off. This helps clear up your infection and relieve your symptoms.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are mild and happen right where you apply the cream. These can include vaginal burning, itching, or irritation. Some women may also notice mild stomach cramps or a feeling of pelvic pressure.
warnings: Do not use this medication if you are in your first trimester of pregnancy without talking to your doctor first. Avoid sexual intercourse while using this cream, as it can weaken latex condoms and diaphragms, making them less effective. If your symptoms do not improve within 3 days or completely go away within 7 days, call your doctor because you may have a different type of infection that needs different treatment.
typical_dosing: The most common dosing is a single dose — you insert one full applicator of cream (about 5 grams) into your vagina at bedtime, just once. Some formulations may require one applicator inserted at bedtime for 3 consecutive nights. Always follow the instructions on your specific product or as directed by your doctor.
